The Electoral College reflects the fact that the US is a republic.  The Founders wanted a constitutional system based on the consent of the governed, but they wanted filtering mechanisms so that the will of the people would be channeled towards the public good.  And they wanted the role of the states respected.  

The EC also guarantees that in an “extended republic” like the US, a candidate cannot just run up the score in one region of the country.

In our time, the EC serves to produce a clearer and more decisive winner (see, eg, Bill Clinton winning 43% of the popular vote but a strong majority in the EC) and focuses election administration in individual states, which reduces complexity in a close race.  

We should be doing more to bolster federalism and the role states play, not further weaken them.  

There is no reason to change the Electoral College.

posts.text:
In March 2026, during his confirmation hearing, Markwayne Mullin fought back tears in front of the chamber as he shared a story about his 15-year-old son, Jim, and a side of Donald Trump rarely seen in the headlines.
​Jim was a strong, gifted wrestler—his father’s whole world—until a severe brain injury changed everything in an instant. When Jim opened his eyes, he didn't recognize his own parents. To the boy Markwayne had watched grow up every single day, his own father looked like a complete stranger.
​According to Mullin’s testimony, the only thing Jim still remembered was that Donald Trump was President.
​When Trump found out, he didn't issue a press release or send a standard card. Mullin recounted how Trump personally called, sent his private plane to fly Jim to a rehabilitation center in California, and called the teenager every single day for two weeks while in the middle of a campaign.
​When it came time for Trump to depart during a visit, his staff repeatedly told him they needed to leave. Twice, Trump told them, "Not yet." The third time, he looked at his team and said, "I guarantee you that plane isn't leaving for at least 15 more minutes."
​He walked inside, sat beside Jim, took his hand, and said: "Do you know why I love your dad? Because he loves you."
​Mullin credited that visit and those words with helping spark the return of his son's memory. Speaking through tears before the committee, Mullin summed it up simply: "He did not do it for publicity. He did it because he cared."
​No cameras. No press conference. Just someone choosing to pause a schedule and sit beside a 15-year-old boy when he had every reason to keep moving.
​Keeping Jim Mullin and his continued recovery in our prayers tonight. 🙏🇺🇸
​#MarkwayneMullin #JimMullin #Inspiration #Fatherhood

Sam Altman says OpenAI will aim its robotics program at building its own data centers.

Speaking on Stripe co-founder John Collison’s Cheeky Pint podcast, he said self-replicating data centers are now “within grasp”: AI-controlled robots running chip factories and building turbines, solar panels and more data centers, to produce “a lot of really cheap compute.”

He argued robots could also make the parts that permits and supply chains hold up today, and said OpenAI already has its own chip and is learning to build its own data centers.

On the cost of AI, Altman said it takes about $70 billion to build and run one gigawatt of capacity for five years, and that $20 billion would make him “much happier.”

NVIDIA reportedly helped AI startups buy its own GPUs instead of lowering prices and selling its excess stock cheaper.

According to a new report, former CEO Jensen Huang used NVIDIA’s money to fund AI startups and data centers so they could keep buying its chips.

The problem is that NVIDIA had ordered far more chips and memory from TSMC than the market could actually use.

CFO Colette Kress pushed back against these deals, even cutting a planned $250 billion commitment to OpenAI down to $125 billion.

If true, NVIDIA may have been helping keep GPU prices high instead of letting excess supply make them cheaper.

Slight underperformance of engines on this flight is the reason. The booster is meant to land with tiny residuals, so the solution is to improve engine performance and performance consistency (underway with Raptor V3.2), as well as adjust flight software to do MECO1 about one second earlier to ensure enough propellant for boostback and landing (tiny change).

These early ships and boosters are already outdated by improved designs in production or on the test stand, so this booster loss does not change our timeline to reach high volume, fully reusable Starship flights.
